1. (S) SITUATION:
{TaskForceFlagshipName} has been detached from the main force to hold the Sunda approaches while coalition shipping clears south. A Soviet-led raider group is moving through the strait, and a Kilo class submarine is assessed in the area. The passage must remain open long enough for the traffic to escape.
2. (S) MISSION: 2.1 Destroy the enemy raider group. 2.2 Destroy any enemy submarine encountered. 2.3 {TaskForceFlagshipName} must survive.
3. (S) EXECUTION: 3.1 Hold the marked Sunda Strait station and maintain awareness of both the raider axis and the shipping route. 3.2 Engage the enemy surface group before it can close the withdrawing coalition traffic. 3.3 Investigate and prosecute the submarine contact at datum A01 if encountered and if the tactical situation permits. 3.4 Withdraw through the marked exit after the raiders are neutralized. Do not remain on station after the passage is clear.
4. (S) ENEMY SITUATION: 4.1 The raider group includes surface combatants and an attached auxiliary operating in or near the strait. 4.2 A Kilo class submarine may approach from the north and use the narrows for concealment.
5. (S) FRIENDLY SITUATION: 5.1 {TaskForceFlagshipName} is the only detached escort assigned to the picket mission. 5.2 Coalition shipping is clearing south and cannot provide meaningful tactical support. 5.3 The main force will rejoin the detached unit after the passage has been secured.
6. (S) INTEL ASSESSMENT: 6.1 Night conditions favor radar action but coastal haze and current shear may complicate maneuvering. 6.2 The enemy may attempt to bypass the picket rather than accept a close engagement. Maintain coverage of the exit. 6.3 Preserve the ship after achieving the surface objective. A surviving escort is more valuable than an extended pursuit.
